newsitem.title: UK: Bass says TV alcopop ad targets over 18s.
newsitem.headline: Bass says TV alcopop ad targets over 18s.

text.p: Bass Plc, the British drinks company which launched the first television commercial for an "alcopop" last month, on Monday said the adverts for Hooper's Hooch are designed to appeal only to drinkers over 18, although some have been broadcast before 9 p.m.

The television ad campaign for Hooper's Hooch -- one of more than 90 of the highly sweetened, fruit-flavoured beverages dubbed alcopops -- launched on December 8 with a 10-second, teaser ad. Full commercials, including two, 20-second adverts, began running on December 9. The ad campaign, designed by the Euro RSCG Wnek Gosper ad agency and which feature "Hooch man" -- a rugged, unshaven man -- will end on January 11.
"This is a first time a flavoured, alcoholic beverage has been seen on television," a Bass spokeswoman told Reuters.

"Hoopers Hooch has taken the drinks industry by storm," the spokeswoman said, noting the beverage had reached a stage where additional advertising was needed to reinforce the brand and help broaden its appeal.
"Our target audience is 18 to 24. We're trying to broaden that, to appeal to people in their 30s and to appeal to men," the spokeswoman said.
The first advert for Hooper's Hooch was aired during "Brookside," the Channel 4 series which broadcasts before the 9 p.m. watershed for adult material on British television.

But Bass is confident it has conformed to regulations governing television commercials for alcohol and said the ads -- and the programmes on which they were shown -- do not appeal to under-age drinkers.

"We're satisfied that all the guidelines that are set by the Advertising Standards Authority and the Broadcast Advertising Clearance Centre, which regulates when our ads are put out, were met," the spokeswoman said.

Hooper's Hooch was one of four Bass brands to launch television ad campaigns during the holiday season, and the spokeswoman said some ads for the three other beverages were also broadcast before 9 p.m.
She declined to detail the amount spent on the TV ads for Hooper's, but said a total of five million pounds is being spent on marketing and advertising the brand in 1996/97.
Hooper's commands a 70 percent share of the 350 million pound alcopop market in Britain. The market is forecast to rise to 500 million pounds in 1997.
"We'll be looking to keep that 70 percent (market share)," the Bass spokeswoman said.

The effectiveness of the TV ads will not be fully evaluated until about two months after the campaign ends on January 11. The spokeswoman said she could not comment on whether Bass might run other television ads for Hooper's later in 1997.
